the-mad-podcast-with-matt-turck.name: The MAD Podcast with Matt Turck
the-mad-podcast-with-matt-turck.bio: Podcast: Cloudflare CEO: Bot Takeover, Edge AI & The Hard Decision Every CEO Will Face

html_en:
Bots now outnumber humans on the internet, AI agents are quietly reshaping how software gets built and used, and regulators are starting to pay attention — a trifecta of signals that the industry's assumptions are due for an update.

🤖 The Bot Majority: A Milestone Nobody Was Ready For

The most striking data point of the day came from Matthew Prince, cofounder and CEO of Cloudflare, in a conversation with Matt Turck on the MAD Podcast. Bot traffic, driven almost entirely by AI agents and crawlers, has officially passed human traffic on the internet — ahead of every projection Cloudflare had made.

"Last fall, in the fall of twenty twenty five, I was asked at what point will automated traffic pass human traffic? We extrapolated the trends and thought it was going to be the end of twenty twenty seven. Fast forward to March 2026 — it moved to the first half of twenty twenty seven. And then my team came to me just a few weeks ago and said, won't believe it, but we actually had bot traffic pass human traffic in the first half of twenty twenty six." — Matthew Prince

The mechanism is intuitive once you see it: an AI agent shopping for a digital camera might visit 5,000 websites where a human would visit five. Multiply that across every agentic workflow running today and the math stops being surprising. Prince's projection from here is remarkable:

"In five years, you might have a thousand times as much traffic on the internet as you do today. I'd take the over on that." — Matthew Prince

The deeper problem is structural. The internet's 28-year-old advertising business model depends on human eyeballs. Bots don't click on ads. As Prince puts it, "the business model of the Internet is gonna change radically" — and what it changes to remains entirely undefined. Watch/Listen: Cloudflare CEO: Bot Takeover, Edge AI & The Hard Decision Every CEO Will Face

💻 Codex Is Eating OpenAI From the Inside Out

If you want to understand how agentic AI tools spread inside organizations, look no further than what's happening at OpenAI itself. Thomas Sottiaux posted a chart that tells the story cleanly: Codex adoption at OpenAI exploded after February 2nd — the release date of the Codex App — and the growth came almost entirely from outside engineering.

"February 2nd was the release of the Codex App. You can see what it did to adoption outside of engineering." — @thsottiaux

The implication: once a coding agent becomes genuinely usable via a consumer-grade interface, non-engineers adopt it fast. Peter Yang offered a vivid personal illustration — he had Codex use a browser to navigate Google Flights and hotel websites, scrape prices, and compile everything into a doc for a Japan trip. "I should just tell it to book everything next," he noted. The gap between "AI assistant" and "AI agent that just does the thing" is closing fast.

🏗️ Building for the Agentic Stack: Apple, Vercel, and the Infrastructure Layer

Two product moves today point to where serious AI infrastructure investment is flowing. Anthropic quietly announced Foundation Models framework support for Claude via a new Swift package — letting Apple developers route complex tasks from Apple's on-device models directly to Claude when the job requires multi-step reasoning or web search. The architecture is elegant: Apple handles fast, local, typed outputs; Claude handles the hard stuff. One seamless experience for the user, backed by whichever model is appropriate at each step.

Meanwhile, Guillermo Rauch at Vercel is thinking about how coding agents inherit design taste. His post on "imbuing coding agents with design standards" gestures at a real unsolved problem: agents will write code that works, but will they write code that looks right? Rauch also flagged a striking platform trend — Grok's image video model has surged to ~50% of all videos generated through Vercel's AI Gateway.

"Grok Imagine Video has become the clear leader in @vercel AI Gateway, now amounting to ~50% of videos generated by developers 🤯" — @rauchg

⚖️ Regulation's Prisoner's Dilemma

The most thoughtful policy framing of the day came from Aaron Levie of Box, who laid out why AI regulation is genuinely hard — not as a deflection, but as a game-theoretic reality.

"AI regulation is far less simple than it looks. It's a prisoner's dilemma at insane scale. If the US remains at the frontier at all times and has heavy regulation on the release of intelligence, we get an economic and geopolitical edge because we can control who has access to frontier intelligence. If we delay model releases, however, and another player — specifically China — doesn't slow down and has equally strong models, then our delays end up advantaging their models and eventually their tech stack." — @levie

Levie identifies open weights as one clear winner in a regulated environment — sovereign AI strategies will need a foundation they can actually control, and open models are the obvious candidate. The bear case he flags is subtle but important: the rapid-fire back-and-forth of incremental model releases may have been necessary for the innovation flywheel, not just a feature of the current moment. Slowing that cadence to accommodate review processes might mean we never find out what we missed.

💡 The Software Company in Crisis

One tweet from Aditya Agarwal captured a quiet anxiety running through the builder community right now:

"It is stupidly hard to start a pure software company right now. Customers don't want software, they want outcomes. So you end up having to do a lot of custom work for them. Anything horizontal is on a ticking clock. Every customer wants to deeply customize. There are opportunities. But you need to have a very heretical 2-3 year view of the world in order to build something good." — @adityaag

It rhymes with a separate observation from Zara Zhang: "Building is getting cheaper, attention is getting more expensive." In a world where the software itself is commoditizing, the moat shifts to distribution, trust, and the ability to tell a story that makes customers believe you'll still be around in three years. That's a harder problem than it sounds.
html_zh:
今天的主题是：AI正在全面渗透基础设施、开发工具和监管框架——而这一切发生的速度，比业界任何人预料的都要快。

🤖 机器人已超越人类：互联网的历史性转折点

本周最震撼的数据来自 Cloudflare。在 Watch/Listen: The MAD Podcast with Matt Turck — Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince 中，Matthew Prince 披露了一个令人瞠目的里程碑：

"我们实际上在2026年上半年就已经看到机器人流量超过了人类流量……如果把这个趋势外推，五年后互联网上的流量可能是今天的一千倍。"
— Matthew Prince, Cloudflare CEO

更惊人的是时间线的压缩速度：Prince 在2025年秋天还预测机器人超越人类要等到2027年底，到2026年3月已提前到2027年上半年，而仅仅数周后，这件事就已经发生了。他解释了原因——AI代理的行为方式与人类截然不同：

"如果我自己去购买数码相机，我可能会浏览五个网站，而我的代理可能会访问5000个——这就是推动流量激增的根本原因。"

随之而来的是一个根本性的商业模式危机：机器人不点广告。互联网沿用了28年的广告模式，正面临颠覆。"未来五年，互联网的商业模式将发生根本性变化，但变成什么，目前完全未知。"

💻 Codex 蔓延：从工程师到全公司

OpenAI 内部的 Codex 使用数据，正在成为最有说服力的产品传道材料。@thsottiaux 分享了一张图表，显示 2月2日 Codex App 发布后，非工程部门的使用率出现了明显跃升：

"2月2日是 Codex App 发布的日子。你可以看到它对工程部门以外的使用率产生了什么影响。"
— @thsottiaux

与此同时，@petergyang 展示了 Codex 在消费场景中的日常应用——他让 Codex 用浏览器导航 Google Flights 和酒店网站，自动整理日本之行的机票和酒店价格并保存为文档。他感慨道："下次我应该直接让它把所有东西都订好。"

不过 Codex 的用户体验仍有粗糙之处。Peter 抱怨在手机上只能通过一个自制的 iPhone 快捷方式访问 Codex，"这感觉很奇怪"——暗示产品的分发渠道尚未追上能力本身的成熟度。

🛠️ 开发者工具：AI 原生体验的新标准

Guillermo Rauch 带来了两则值得关注的产品信号。其一，Next.js 推出了带有"复制提示词"按钮的错误修复建议功能，他称之为"代理式艺术品"——这是开发工具 AI 原生化的一个精妙缩影。其二，他分享了 Vercel 如何将设计标准注入编程代理的方法论。

在模型分发层面，Rauch 指出 Grok 的视频生成功能已占据 Vercel AI Gateway 约50%的视频生成量，成为开发者中最受欢迎的视频模型——这对其他竞争者是个不小的警示。

Anthropic 这边也有新动作：Claude 现已支持 Apple Foundation Models 框架，通过一个 Swift 包，开发者可以在 iOS 27/macOS 27 上将本地模型处理不了的复杂任务无缝交给 Claude 完成——"对用户来说是同一个体验，背后是最合适的模型在各司其职。"

⚖️ AI 监管：囚徒困境，国家尺度

Aaron Levie 用一篇长推文，把当前 AI 监管困境分析得入木三分。他的核心论点是：我们已经进入了"事实上的AI监管"时代，但这个博弈没有简单的解法：

"如果美国延迟模型发布，而另一个参与者——尤其是中国——没有放慢脚步，并拥有同样强大的模型（现在还没有，但很快？），那么我们的延迟最终会让他们的模型受益，乃至最终让他们的技术栈占优。"
— Aaron Levie

他还指出了一个意想不到的赢家：开源权重模型。在闭源模型受到审查的背景下，开放模型成为各国主权AI战略的首选基础，其战略价值正在被重新估量。

💡 创业者的生存焦虑：纯软件公司越来越难做

最后，@adityaag 的一段感慨，精准击中了当下许多 SaaS 创业者的心声：

"现在创办一家纯软件公司难得出奇。客户不想要软件，他们想要结果。所以你最终不得不为他们做大量定制化工作。任何水平层面的产品都在倒计时。你需要对未来两三年的世界持有一个非常'异端'的看法，才能做出好东西。"
— @adityaag

这与 Cloudflare CEO 关于互联网商业模式颠覆的判断遥相呼应：当基础假设在动摇，押注现有范式的人，风险正在悄悄累积。
